newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST-HUNGARY GOVT. SECURITIES YIELDS SEEN DOWN.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-HUNGARY GOVT. SECURITIES YIELDS SEEN DOWN.

text.p: Hungarian government security yields are likely to drop slightly in the next two weeks, helped by a probable government decision on an anti-inflation programme for 1998, dealers said on Tuesday.

The government is likely to choose on Thursday between two alternative programmes, one aimed at an inflation cut to some 10 percent in year-on-year terms for December 1998, and the other targeting levels of about 13 percent.
Inflation ran at 18.6 percent in April and the government expects it to go down to some 17 percent by December.
Dealers said the government was more likely to approve the less radical inflation reduction programme.
"Even the 13 percent target may be revised upward as GDP (gross domestic product) growth is picking up and a larger inflation cut may be seen as jeopardising it," said Zsolt Bango of Gog Securities.

If the government adopts the moderate programme, government bond yields are likely to drop by 0.1 to 0.2 percentage points in the next two weeks, while the approval of the alternative programme would trigger an even larger fall, dealers said.
"The two-year bond yield could go down 20 basis points if there is an anti-inflation programme," Karoly Misky of interbank trader Bondtrade Securities said.

However, discount Treasury bill yields are likely to change little until the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) cuts its reverse repo rates -- which have up to one month maturity -- or its six and twelve-month deposit rates, dealers said.
Hungarian T-bills have maturities of up to one year.
One dealer said that according to market talk the NBH may issue a new one-year bond in the next two weeks, and the yield it offers could influence the government bond market.
